<a id="prelude"></a>
## Built-in functions (no import needed)

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| `print(*values, sep = " ", end = "\n")` | Write values to the output, separated by `sep`. |
| `len(x)` | Number of items in a str, list, map, range, vec or table. |
| `type(x)` | Type name as a string: "int", "str", "list", or the class name. |
| `str(x)` | Text form of any value. |
| `repr(x)` | Text form with strings quoted. |
| `int(x, base = 10)` | Whole number from a number or a string. |
| `float(x)` | Decimal number from a number or a string. |
| `bool(x)` | Truth value of x. |
| `list(x)` | List from a range, str, map (keys), vec or table (rows). |
| `range(start, end, step = 1)` | Numbers from start up to (not including) end. range(n) is 0..n. |
| `abs(x)` | Absolute value. |
| `min(*values, key = nil, default = nil)` | Smallest value (of many args, or of one list). |
| `max(*values, key = nil, default = nil)` | Largest value (of many args, or of one list). |
| `sum(xs, start = 0)` | Sum of items; float lists use compensated summation. |
| `round(x, ndigits = nil)` | Round half to even. With ndigits gives a float. |
| `sorted(xs, key = nil, reverse = false)` | New sorted list. |
| `reversed(xs)` | New list in reverse order. |
| `enumerate(xs, start = 0)` | List of [index, item] pairs. |
| `zip(*lists)` | List of rows taking one item from each list. |
| `any(xs)` | True if any item is truthy. |
| `all(xs)` | True if every item is truthy. |
| `input(prompt = nil)` | Read one line from the keyboard (nil at end of input). |
| `error(message, kind = "Error")` | Make an error value; use with `throw`. |
| `assert(cond, message = nil)` | Throw AssertionError when cond is false. |
| `env(name, default = nil)` | Environment variable (also read from .env). |
| `args()` | Command line arguments after `mpp run file.mpp --`. |
| `exit(code = 0)` | Stop the program. |
| `warn(*values)` | Print a warning to stderr. |
| `chr(code)` | Character for a Unicode code point. |
| `ord(ch)` | Unicode code point of one character. |
| `copy(x)` | Shallow copy of a list, map or instance. |
| `isinstance(x, type)` | True if x is an instance of a class (or has the given type name). |
| `callable(x)` | True if x can be called. |
| `skip(reason = "")` | Skip the running test block. |
| `expect_throws(fn, kind = nil, contains = nil)` | Call fn; it must throw (optionally of `kind`, message containing `contains`). Returns the error. |
| `expect_snapshot(value, name = nil)` | Compare value with its saved snapshot; first run saves it. |
| `note(*values)` | Add a note line to the test report. |
| `vec(xs)` | Fast number vector; nil becomes NaN (missing). |
| `linspace(lo, hi, n = 50)` | n evenly spaced numbers from lo to hi. |
| `table(data)` | Table from a map of columns or a list of row maps. |
| `load_csv(path, sep = ",")` | Load a CSV/TSV file as a table, guessing column types. |
| `load_jsonl(path)` | Load a JSON-lines file (one object per line) as a table. |
| `load_json(path)` | Load a JSON file (list of rows or map of columns) as a table. |
| `plot(data, x, y, title = nil, log = false)` | Line chart of table (or training log) columns; shows in HTML reports. |

## Module `math`

`import math`

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| `math.sqrt(x)` | Square root. |
| `math.exp(x)` | e to the power x. |
| `math.log(x, base = e)` | Logarithm. |
| `math.log2(x)` | Base-2 logarithm. |
| `math.log10(x)` | Base-10 logarithm. |
| `math.log1p(x)` | log(1 + x), accurate for small x. |
| `math.expm1(x)` | exp(x) - 1, accurate for small x. |
| `math.sin(x)` | Sine (radians). |
| `math.cos(x)` | Cosine (radians). |
| `math.tan(x)` | Tangent (radians). |
| `math.asin(x)` | Arc sine. |
| `math.acos(x)` | Arc cosine. |
| `math.atan(x)` | Arc tangent. |
| `math.atan2(y, x)` | Angle of the point (x, y). |
| `math.sinh(x)` | Hyperbolic sine. |
| `math.cosh(x)` | Hyperbolic cosine. |
| `math.tanh(x)` | Hyperbolic tangent. |
| `math.erf(x)` | Error function. |
| `math.erfc(x)` | Complementary error function. |
| `math.gamma(x)` | Gamma function. |
| `math.lgamma(x)` | Log of the gamma function. |
| `math.floor(x)` | Round down to a whole number. |
| `math.ceil(x)` | Round up to a whole number. |
| `math.trunc(x)` | Drop the fraction. |
| `math.pow(x, y)` | x to the power y, as a float. |
| `math.hypot(x, y)` | sqrt(x*x + y*y). |
| `math.isnan(x)` | True if x is NaN. |
| `math.isinf(x)` | True if x is infinite. |
| `math.isfinite(x)` | True if x is a normal number. |
| `math.clamp(x, lo, hi)` | x limited to [lo, hi]. |
| `math.sign(x)` | -1, 0 or 1. |
| `math.gcd(a, b)` | Greatest common divisor. |
| `math.factorial(n)` | n! as an int. |
| `math.comb(n, k)` | Number of ways to choose k of n. |
| `math.pi` | 3.14159... |
| `math.e` | 2.71828... |
| `math.tau` | 2 * pi. |
| `math.inf` | Positive infinity. |
| `math.nan` | Not a number. |

<a id="stats"></a>
## Module `stats`

`import stats`

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| `stats.mean(x)` | Average. |
| `stats.median(x)` | Middle value. |
| `stats.sum(x)` | Sum (compensated). |
| `stats.min(x)` | Smallest value. |
| `stats.max(x)` | Largest value. |
| `stats.skew(x)` | Skewness (population, like scipy). |
| `stats.kurtosis(x)` | Excess kurtosis (population, like scipy). |
| `stats.sem(x)` | Standard error of the mean. |
| `stats.var(x, ddof = 1)` | Variance (sample by default). |
| `stats.std(x, ddof = 1)` | Standard deviation (sample by default). |
| `stats.quantile(x, q)` | Quantile(s), linear interpolation; q can be a list. |
| `stats.iqr(x)` | Interquartile range. |
| `stats.mad(x)` | Median absolute deviation. |
| `stats.zscore(x)` | Standardised values as a vec. |
| `stats.describe(x)` | count, missing, mean, std, min, p25, median, p75, max. |
| `stats.ci_mean(x, level = 0.95)` | t confidence interval for the mean. |
| `stats.ttest(a, b, equal_var = false, alternative = "two-sided", level = 0.95)` | Two-sample t-test (Welch by default): statistic, p_value, df, diff (a - b), ci, cohens_d. |
| `stats.ttest_ind(a, b, equal_var = false, alternative = "two-sided", level = 0.95)` | Same as ttest. |
| `stats.ttest_1samp(x, mu = 0, alternative = "two-sided", level = 0.95)` | One-sample t-test against mu. |
| `stats.ttest_rel(a, b, alternative = "two-sided", level = 0.95)` | Paired t-test. |
| `stats.ztest(x, mu = 0, sigma = nil, alternative = "two-sided", level = 0.95)` | z-test for a mean (sigma known, or sample sd). |
| `stats.chi2(table, correction = true)` | Chi-square test of independence on a contingency table; also cramers_v, expected. |
| `stats.chi2_gof(observed, expected = nil)` | Chi-square goodness of fit (expected defaults to equal). |
| `stats.fisher(table, alternative = "two-sided")` | Fisher exact test on a 2x2 table. |
| `stats.mannwhitney(a, b, alternative = "two-sided", method = nil)` | Mann-Whitney U (exact for small samples without ties, else normal approx). |
| `stats.wilcoxon(a, b = nil, alternative = "two-sided", method = nil)` | Wilcoxon signed-rank test (paired, or one sample against 0). |
| `stats.ks(a, b, method = nil)` | Two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test. |
| `stats.anova(*groups)` | One-way ANOVA; also eta_squared. |
| `stats.kruskal(*groups)` | Kruskal-Wallis H test. |
| `stats.levene(*groups, center = "median")` | Equal-variance test (Brown-Forsythe by default). |
| `stats.shapiro(x)` | Shapiro-Wilk normality test. |
| `stats.pearson(x, y, alternative = "two-sided", level = 0.95)` | Pearson correlation r with p_value and CI. |
| `stats.spearman(x, y, alternative = "two-sided")` | Spearman rank correlation. |
| `stats.kendall(x, y)` | Kendall tau-b. |
| `stats.linregress(x, y)` | Simple linear regression: slope, intercept, r, p_value, stderr. |
| `stats.ols(data, formula, names = nil, intercept = true, level = 0.95)` | Least squares: ols(table, "y ~ a + b") or ols(y, [x1, x2]). Coefficients with se, t, p, ci; r2, adj_r2, f. |
| `stats.cohens_d(a, b)` | Standardised mean difference (pooled sd). |
| `stats.hedges_g(a, b)` | Cohen's d with small-sample correction. |
| `stats.cliffs_delta(a, b)` | Non-parametric effect size in [-1, 1]. |
| `stats.odds_ratio(table, level = 0.95)` | Odds ratio of a 2x2 table with CI. |
| `stats.relative_risk(table, level = 0.95)` | Risk ratio of a 2x2 table with CI. |
| `stats.bootstrap(x, fn = "mean", n = 10000, level = 0.95, method = "bca")` | Bootstrap CI for any statistic (name or function). |
| `stats.bootstrap_diff(a, b, fn = "mean", n = 10000, level = 0.95)` | Bootstrap CI and p for fn(b) - fn(a). |
| `stats.permutation_test(a, b, fn = "mean", n = 10000, alternative = "two-sided")` | Permutation test of fn(a) - fn(b). |
| `stats.adjust(p_values, method = "holm")` | Multiple-testing correction: bonferroni, holm, hochberg, bh, by. |
| `stats.norm_cdf(x, mean = 0, sd = 1)` | Normal CDF. |
| `stats.norm_ppf(p, mean = 0, sd = 1)` | Normal quantile. |
| `stats.norm_pdf(x, mean = 0, sd = 1)` | Normal density. |
| `stats.t_cdf(x, df)` | Student t CDF. |
| `stats.t_ppf(p, df)` | Student t quantile. |
| `stats.chi2_cdf(x, df)` | Chi-square CDF. |
| `stats.chi2_ppf(p, df)` | Chi-square quantile. |
| `stats.f_sf(x, d1, d2)` | F distribution upper tail. |
| `stats.beta_cdf(x, a, b)` | Beta CDF. |
| `stats.beta_ppf(p, a, b)` | Beta quantile. |
| `stats.binom_pmf(k, n, p)` | Binomial probability of exactly k. |
| `stats.binom_cdf(k, n, p)` | Binomial probability of at most k. |
| `stats.poisson_pmf(k, lam)` | Poisson probability of exactly k. |
| `stats.poisson_cdf(k, lam)` | Poisson probability of at most k. |

<a id="ab"></a>
## Module `ab`

`import ab`

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| `ab.proportions(a, b, x_a, n_a, x_b, n_b, alpha = 0.05, alternative = "two-sided")` | Two-proportion z-test from 0/1 data or counts: rate_a, rate_b, diff, ci_diff, lift, ci_lift, p_value, significant. |
| `ab.means(a, b, alpha = 0.05, alternative = "two-sided")` | Welch test on means with lift and lift CI. |
| `ab.ratio(num_a, den_a, num_b, den_b, alpha = 0.05, alternative = "two-sided")` | Ratio metric test (e.g. revenue per session) by delta method. |
| `ab.cuped(y_a, x_a, y_b, x_b, alpha = 0.05, alternative = "two-sided")` | CUPED variance reduction with a pre-period covariate x. |
| `ab.srm(counts, expected = nil, threshold = 0.001)` | Sample ratio mismatch check: did traffic split as planned? |
| `ab.aa(data, n = 1000, alpha = 0.05, metric = nil)` | A/A simulation: false positive rate should be near alpha. |
| `ab.multi(groups, control = nil, metric = nil, correction = "holm", alpha = 0.05)` | A/B/n: every variant against control, with corrected p-values. |
| `ab.bayes(a, b, x_a, n_a, x_b, n_b, prior = [1, 1], draws = 100000, level = 0.95)` | Bayesian Beta-Binomial: prob_b_better, expected losses, lift CI. |
| `ab.bayes_means(a, b, level = 0.95)` | Bayesian view of a mean difference (normal approximation). |
| `ab.msprt(a, b, tau = nil, alpha = 0.05)` | Mixture sequential test: always-valid p-value, safe to peek. |
| `ab.sequential_bounds(looks = 5, alpha = 0.05, spending = "obrien-fleming", info = nil)` | Group-sequential z boundaries (Lan-DeMets spending). |
| `ab.segments(data, variant, metric, by, control = nil, alpha = 0.05)` | Effect per segment of a table, with a Simpson's paradox warning. |
| `ab.novelty(data, variant, metric, time, control = nil, periods = nil)` | Lift per time period and its trend (fading novelty effect). |
| `ab.guardrail(a, b, margin, relative = false, higher_is_better = true, alpha = 0.05)` | Non-inferiority: B is not worse than A by more than margin. |

`import power`

| Function | What it does |

| `power.achieved_means(sd, diff, n_a, alpha = 0.05, ratio = 1, alternative = "two-sided")` | Power of a mean test. |
| `power.duration(total, daily, share = 1)` | Days (and weeks) needed to reach `total` users. |

## Module `ml`

`import ml`

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| `ml.accuracy(y_true, y_pred)` | Share of correct predictions. |
| `ml.balanced_accuracy(y_true, y_pred)` | Mean recall over classes. |
| `ml.mcc(y_true, y_pred)` | Matthews correlation coefficient. |
| `ml.cohen_kappa(y_true, y_pred)` | Agreement beyond chance. |
| `ml.precision(y_true, y_pred, average = nil, pos_label = 1)` | Precision (binary, macro, micro, weighted or none). |
| `ml.recall(y_true, y_pred, average = nil, pos_label = 1)` | Recall. |
| `ml.f1(y_true, y_pred, average = nil, pos_label = 1)` | F1 score. |
| `ml.fbeta(y_true, y_pred, beta, average = nil, pos_label = 1)` | F-beta score. |
| `ml.confusion_matrix(y_true, y_pred)` | labels and matrix[true][pred]. |
| `ml.classification_report(y_true, y_pred)` | accuracy and a per-class precision/recall/f1/support table. |
| `ml.roc_auc(y_true, scores, pos_label = 1)` | ROC AUC; scores as rows gives one-vs-rest macro AUC. |
| `ml.roc_curve(y_true, scores, pos_label = 1)` | fpr, tpr, thresholds, auc. |
| `ml.pr_curve(y_true, scores, pos_label = 1)` | precision, recall, thresholds, average_precision. |
| `ml.average_precision(y_true, scores, pos_label = 1)` | Area under the precision-recall curve (sklearn definition). |
| `ml.pr_auc(y_true, scores, pos_label = 1)` | Same as average_precision. |
| `ml.log_loss(y_true, probs, pos_label = 1)` | Cross-entropy (binary probs or rows of class probs). |
| `ml.brier(y_true, probs, pos_label = 1)` | Mean squared error of probabilities. |
| `ml.top_k_accuracy(y_true, scores, k = 2)` | True class among the k highest scores. |
| `ml.regression(y_true, y_pred)` | mae, mse, rmse, r2, mape, smape, median_ae, max_error, explained_variance. |
| `ml.mae(y_true, y_pred)` | Mean absolute error. |
| `ml.mse(y_true, y_pred)` | Mean squared error. |
| `ml.rmse(y_true, y_pred)` | Root mean squared error. |
| `ml.r2(y_true, y_pred)` | Coefficient of determination. |
| `ml.mape(y_true, y_pred)` | Mean absolute percentage error. |
| `ml.ndcg(relevance, k = nil, gain = "linear")` | NDCG@k; relevance in ranked order, one list per query. |
| `ml.precision_at_k(relevance, k)` | Share of relevant items in the top k. |
| `ml.recall_at_k(relevance, k)` | Share of relevant items found in the top k. |
| `ml.hit_rate(relevance, k)` | Any relevant item in the top k. |
| `ml.mrr(relevance, k = nil)` | Mean reciprocal rank. |
| `ml.map_at_k(relevance, k)` | Mean average precision at k. |
| `ml.calibration(y_true, probs, bins = 10, strategy = "uniform", pos_label = 1)` | ECE, MCE and a reliability bin table. |
| `ml.psi(reference, current, bins = 10)` | Population stability index and level (none, moderate, major). |
| `ml.wasserstein(a, b)` | Earth mover's distance between two samples. |
| `ml.kl(p, q)` | KL divergence of two distributions (nats). |
| `ml.js(p, q)` | Jensen-Shannon divergence (bits, 0..1). |
| `ml.drift(reference, current, columns = nil, psi_threshold = 0.2, p_threshold = 0.01)` | Per-column drift report between two tables. |
| `ml.fairness(y_true, y_pred, group, pos_label = 1)` | Per-group rates, disparate impact, equal opportunity, equalized odds. |
| `ml.mcnemar(y_true, pred_a, pred_b, exact = nil)` | Do two classifiers differ on the same data? |
| `ml.delong(y_true, scores_a, scores_b, pos_label = 1)` | DeLong test for two correlated AUCs. |
| `ml.paired_bootstrap(y_true, pred_a, pred_b, metric = "accuracy", n = 2000, level = 0.95)` | CI and p for the difference in any metric. |
| `ml.cv5x2(diffs)` | Dietterich 5x2cv paired t-test. |
| `ml.threshold_sweep(y_true, scores, metric = "f1", steps = 101, pos_label = 1)` | Metrics at many thresholds and the best one. |
| `ml.slices(data, y_true, y_pred, by, metric = "accuracy", min_n = 1)` | Metric per slice of a table, worst first. |
| `ml.check(data)` | Missing values, duplicates, constant columns, ranges. |
| `ml.leakage(train, test, columns = nil)` | Rows of test that also appear in train. |
| `ml.label_balance(y)` | Counts, shares and imbalance ratio. |
| `ml.schema(data, spec)` | Check column types: {"age": "number", "name": "text"}. |

<a id="llm"></a>
## Module `llm`

`import llm`

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| `llm.http(url, mode = "openai", api = "chat", model = nil, headers = nil, timeout = 120, field = nil)` | Connect to a model server (OpenAI-style or raw JSON). Extra named args become defaults. |
| `llm.process(command, cwd = nil, timeout = 120)` | Connect to a script that reads/writes one JSON line per request. |
| `llm.mock(fn, name = "mock")` | Fake model: fn(prompt, params) returns the text. |
| `llm.eval_set(model, cases, metric = "exact", threshold = 0.5, concurrency = 4)` | Run a golden set: score, pass_rate, latency, results table. |
| `llm.compare_checkpoints(model_a, model_b, cases, metric = "exact", n_boot = 2000)` | Is B better than A? CI, sign test, verdict, regressions. |
| `llm.determinism(model, prompt, runs = 5)` | Same prompt and settings, same answer? |
| `llm.consistency(model, prompts, metric = "similarity")` | Do paraphrases get the same answer? |
| `llm.judge(model, answer, rubric, question = nil, scale = 10)` | Your model grades an answer: score in [0, 1], rating, raw. |
| `llm.load_test(model, prompts, requests = nil, concurrency = 8)` | Latency percentiles, requests/s, tokens/s, error rate. |
| `llm.latency_stats(ms)` | p50, p90, p95, p99, mean, max of latencies. |
| `llm.exact_match(pred, ref, normalize = true)` | 1 if equal after normalising (lists give the mean). |
| `llm.token_f1(pred, ref)` | SQuAD token F1. |
| `llm.similarity(a, b)` | 1 - edit distance / length. |
| `llm.edit_distance(a, b)` | Levenshtein distance in characters. |
| `llm.contains(text, sub, case_sensitive = false)` | True if text contains sub. |
| `llm.regex_match(text, pattern)` | True if the pattern matches somewhere. |
| `llm.extract(text, pattern, group = nil)` | First match (or capture group), or nil. |
| `llm.extract_all(text, pattern)` | All matches. |
| `llm.json_valid(text)` | True if text is valid JSON. |
| `llm.parse_json(text)` | JSON found in a reply (code fences and prose allowed), or nil. |
| `llm.json_schema(value, schema)` | Check JSON (text or value) against a schema: valid, errors. |
| `llm.bleu(candidate, references, max_n = 4, smooth = false)` | Sentence BLEU (nltk). |
| `llm.rouge(candidate, reference)` | rouge1, rouge2, rougeL F-scores. |
| `llm.rouge_l(pred, ref)` | ROUGE-L F-score. |
| `llm.rouge_n(candidate, reference, n = 1)` | ROUGE-N precision, recall, f1. |
| `llm.chrf(candidate, references)` | chrF score 0..100 (sacrebleu). |
| `llm.refusal(text)` | True if the text looks like a refusal. |
| `llm.pass_at_k(n, correct, k)` | Unbiased pass@k estimate. |
| `llm.perplexity_of(logprobs)` | exp(-mean logprob). |
| `llm.train_log(path)` | Load a training log (JSONL/CSV, or a table). |
| `llm.check_training(log, loss = nil, val_loss = nil, step = nil, grad_norm = nil, lr = nil, throughput = nil, window = 50)` | Find training problems: healthy, problems, issues table, summary. |
| `llm.compare_runs(a, b, metric = nil)` | Compare two training runs over shared steps. |
| `llm.plot(data, x, y, title = nil, log = false)` | Line chart (same as the global plot). |
